title: The non-Cohen–Macaulay construction
known: The fibre-product exact sequence and its extra Tor term are checked in this run. The gap is earlier: normality and failure of Cohen–Macaulayness do not alone isolate the bad locus sufficiently for the intended hypersurface choice. Stacks00RD gives the standard finite-type openness context, but does not supply the missing projective input.
residual: A precise example with the intended unusual change in the non-Cohen–Macaulay locus, including every geometric existence choice and local depth calculation.
would_establish: A precise example with the intended unusual change in the non-Cohen–Macaulay locus, including every geometric existence choice and local depth calculation.
first_step: Specify the desired dimension and isolated bad locus on the projective scheme, then find one explicit normal projective example whose local cohomology is computable. A useful first run can finish that example or demonstrate that the proposed dimension pattern is incompatible with the chosen geometry.
rating_qualification: Progress rates a bounded deliverable, not resolution of the broad program.

title: Broad Cohen lifting
known: Stacks07NN/09Q9 supply the local complete flat regular-fibre factorization. The relative pro-Tor comparison is reconstructed in proof_notes.md. These results do not automatically establish the draft’s arbitrary topological algebra version or its global uniqueness claims.
residual: The strongest nonlocal lifting statement actually supported by the draft, separated from established complete local Cohen factorization.
would_establish: The strongest nonlocal lifting statement actually supported by the draft, separated from established complete local Cohen factorization.
first_step: Write an exact diagram of rings and topologies from the relevant scan and list which completeness, locality, finiteness and residue-separability hypotheses are used at each lift. Test the weakest missing hypothesis on a product or localization example.
rating_qualification: Progress rates a bounded deliverable, not resolution of the broad program.

title: Finite-order natural functors
known: The smooth-manifold equivalence in Kolár–Michor–Slovák §§14.6,14.8 is an exact analogue. The manuscript’s scheme category and Greenberg-style extension have not been identified with a theorem of that scope.
residual: A valid scheme-theoretic equivalence between finite-order natural constructions and actions of a finite jet or principal-parts group, under explicit base and locality conditions.
would_establish: A valid scheme-theoretic equivalence between finite-order natural constructions and actions of a finite jet or principal-parts group, under explicit base and locality conditions.
first_step: Restrict to smooth affine schemes of one fixed relative dimension over a characteristic-zero field, make the locality axiom explicit, and compare the representing jet group with the bitorsor already constructed. This isolates a tractable statement before any arbitrary-base extension.
rating_qualification: Progress rates a bounded deliverable, not resolution of the broad program.

title: The withdrawn compactness proposition
known: The original linear-variety proof is invalid and the1967 errata expressly withdraw the proposition. The finite-solvability polynomial example checks that proof mechanism only. Successive countable adic lifting has a different argument.
residual: Either a counterexample satisfying the exact hypotheses of withdrawn EGA0.19.3.12, or a corrected theorem with additional countability or topology assumptions.
would_establish: Either a counterexample satisfying the exact hypotheses of withdrawn EGA0.19.3.12, or a corrected theorem with additional countability or topology assumptions.
first_step: Extract the exact original theorem and define its square-open ideals and topology independently of the defective proof. Compare countable versus uncountable inverse systems before attempting a general algebra-lift example. The task should begin from the withdrawal, not by treating the old assertion as established.
rating_qualification: Progress rates a bounded deliverable, not resolution of the broad program.

title: Infinite differential directions
known: The finite-support proofs in this run settle the stated cases. The earlier run’s stronger idea is not silently attributed to the manuscript, and the searches do not establish novelty.
residual: A reusable precise note covering nonsplitting and nonprojectivity of differentials of power-series rings, with the adic and discrete categories visibly separated.
would_establish: A reusable precise note covering nonsplitting and nonprojectivity of differentials of power-series rings, with the adic and discrete categories visibly separated.
first_step: Check the scans’ precise coefficient-field and finite-base-enlargement clauses, then compare the completed proof with modern accounts of noncontinuous derivations. A few-hour run should produce a polished theorem/proof and a bounded prior-literature search, rather than a novelty announcement.
rating_qualification: Progress rates a bounded deliverable, not resolution of the broad program.

title: Meromorphic denominators under restriction
known: Lê’s correction matches the original printed text. Stacks01X1 gives the restriction-stable setup;0EMG restores the familiar identifications for locally noetherian schemes. The separate21.2.9 trivialization issue is already localized.
residual: An explicit nonnoetherian example explaining exactly which stalk or open-set identification fails in the printed EGA20.1 formulation, and which definition is stable under restriction.
would_establish: An explicit nonnoetherian example explaining exactly which stalk or open-set identification fails in the printed EGA20.1 formulation, and which definition is stable under restriction.
first_step: Construct an affine ring and open subset where a section is a nonzerodivisor at the chosen stalk but fails the required neighborhood condition. Check the sheaf and stalk maps explicitly, then use the scans to decide Lê’s intended notation.
rating_qualification: Progress rates a bounded deliverable, not resolution of the broad program.

title: A scan-based errata concordance
known: Several exact correspondences are now established: the withdrawal of0.19.3.12; the locality correction; the sign change with its own old/new-label transposition; the16.1 immersion hypothesis; the19.5.5 proof credited to Deligne; and the Artin XII6.3 draft. The III4.3.6 equality is false, but the conclusion survives an injection-based proof.
residual: A reliable critical apparatus linking Deligne’s letters, the original EGA passages, the later correction list and the final SGA redactions.
would_establish: A reliable critical apparatus linking Deligne’s letters, the original EGA passages, the later correction list and the final SGA redactions.
first_step: Put each manuscript scan beside the corresponding original printed page and decide only the flagged ink questions. A concordance should preserve authorship, dates, cancellations and the distinction between an erratum, a proof simplification and a changed hypothesis.
rating_qualification: Progress is for one bounded run. Any ink collation requires the missing scans; current numeric rating includes that access limit.

title: Lang’s alleged gap
known: Jouanolou points specifically to separability of a completion fraction field. Nagata’s1957 note removes a normic-form assumption in related C_i results, which is not enough to identify this analytic gap. The original Lang proof has not been read in this run.
residual: The exact missing step alleged in Jouanolou’s1963 offprint and whether Lang’s own argument or later corrections already handle it.
would_establish: The exact missing step alleged in Jouanolou’s1963 offprint and whether Lang’s own argument or later corrections already handle it.
first_step: Obtain the original1952 paper, locate the convergent-series/complete-valued-field argument, and trace every use of separability. Report a proof comparison with exact pages, even if the outcome is that Jouanolou’s allegation cannot be confirmed.
rating_qualification: Progress rates a bounded deliverable, not resolution of the broad program.

title: One quotient or bundle problem from cote26
known: Modern algebraic-space and stack representability answers many constrained versions. Nonprojective duality and unpolarized abelian deformations are established. Arbitrary varieties, arbitrary affine structural groups and “without fixed points” remain too broad or ambiguous to be one theorem.
residual: A modern theorem or counterexample for one exact question, such as the quotient of a specified free flat group action or bundles over a fixed relative curve.
would_establish: A modern theorem or counterexample for one exact question, such as the quotient of a specified free flat group action or bundles over a fixed relative curve.
first_step: Choose a single row in MP48–58, fix the moduli functor and topology, and compare its hypotheses with the exact opened theorem. For the relative P1 question, begin with a two-stratum family where splitting type changes, so that the limitation of fibrewise classification is visible.
rating_qualification: Progress rates a bounded deliverable, not resolution of the broad program.

first_step: Decide the two missing hypotheses on the scans. Then state each corrected implication with a single grading convention and attach the saved minimal counterexample to the literal alternative. This is an editorial and expository task; no novelty claim is indicated.
rating_qualification: Progress is for one bounded run. Any ink collation requires the missing scans; current numeric rating includes that access limit.
